messages:
sarah-sales: FYI customer in POC lab (Windows corp proxy + strict firewall) reporting timeouts on streaming responses. Both our TS demo and their Python client stall after a few tokens. Anyone run into proxy + keepAlive weirdness? attaching short logs below. :confused:

ben-eng: @sarah-sales can you paste the client-side stack / error? Is it a socket hangup or TLS handshake? Also which SDK versions?

sarah-sales: SDKs: ts-sdk v0.14.2, py-sdk 1.1.0. Error snippets from their env: 

```
Error: socket hang up
    at connResetException (internal/errors.js:610:14)
    at TLSSocket.socketCloseListener (_http_client.js:508:21)
Caused by: ECONNRESET during streaming chunk write
```

They also see repeated: 
`request timeout after 30s` and occasional `write EPIPE` in the server-side proxy logs.

mike-se: Two quick suspects: (1) corporate proxy is terminating idle keep-alive connections and not handling chunked transfer streaming well, (2) Nagle + small chunk sizes causing delays that trip the proxy's per-connection timers.

tia-qa: +1. We saw similar with older HTTP proxies that don't like long-lived streaming requests with tiny chunks. Workarounds: increase chunk size, disable socket-level Nagle (TCP_NODELAY), or switch to a polling-style keepalive at app level.

ben-eng: For TS/Node clients you can try forcing socket TCP_NODELAY and tuning agent keepAlive. Example we recommended to a customer: 

```js
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 16 });
// set TCP_NODELAY when socket attaches
agent.on('free', (socket) => socket.setNoDelay && socket.setNoDelay(true));
// axios example
axios.get(url, { httpAgent: agent, timeout: 60000 })
```

Also try disabling HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer on their side if possible (buffer and send larger payloads) or bump client-side read timeouts.

mike-se: For Python clients (requests/urllib3) suggest disabling persistent connections or set pool_block=False and set socket options via urllib3's connection_pool. Quick snippet: 

```py
import requests
s = requests.Session()
s.trust_env = False  # bypass env proxy settings for testing
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=10, pool_maxsize=10, max_retries=3))
resp = s.get(url, stream=True, timeout=(5, 60))
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
    process(chunk)
```

If corp proxy is injecting resets, testing with `trust_env=False` helps determine if their proxy credentials or PAC rules are interfering.

sarah-sales: They tried setting env NO_PROXY but still see resets — their infra team says proxy is transparent and rewrites TLS. They're reluctant to disable proxy. Customer is worried about changing network rules for POC.

ben-eng: Understood. Other lower-friction options: 
- Increase SDK client-side read/stream timeout to 90s to survive proxy stalls.
- Batch tokens on our streaming path to emit larger chunks (we can push a temporary config to staging).
- Offer a patched SDK build that disables connection reuse for streaming requests (falls back to short-lived connections).

tia-qa: I can spin up a repro using our internal proxy VM to emulate the corp appliance. If we can reproduce, we can try two changes: bump chunk size and toggle TCP_NODELAY to show which mitigates resets.

sarah-sales: That would be great — customer ok with us doing remote tests in their lab later today. They'll need clear steps to run our experimental SDK. Any chance of a quick patch we can ship to them?

ben-eng: I can cut a beta: ts-sdk 0.14.3-beta that adds an env flag REDWOOD_STREAM_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE=true which makes streaming requests use short-lived connections + sets socket.setNoDelay(true). I'll push to canary now. deploy-bot: any ETA on canary rollout?

deploy-bot: Canary build for ts-sdk 0.14.3-beta queued. ETA ~12 minutes. I'll post link when available. :rocket:

mike-se: If canary helps, we should prepare a short runbook for the customer: how to set REDWOOD_STREAM_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE, example Node/Python wraps, and metrics to capture (percentage of failed streams, time to first token). I can draft.

ben-eng: Good plan. If the beta reduces resets we can follow up with an SDK patch and a config knob to control chunking/keepalive. Also logging: ask customer to capture client-side `socket.bytesRead/bytesWritten` and proxy logs showing `RST`/`FIN` to correlate.

sarah-sales: Thanks all — I'll coordinate the lab window and share the runbook draft. Will ping when canary link is up. :thumbsup:
